The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

In the provided text, the author’s motive is to explore the themes of human connection and the natural cycle of life and decay through the lens of neglect. This motive is structurally linked to the narrative arc of the sunflower itself. The story begins with the protagonist nurturing the garden, representing vitality and care, but shifts as the sunflower begins to wilt. This physical decline mirrors the protagonist’s internal state of sadness and isolation. By aligning the botanical metaphor of the wilting plant with the protagonist’s emotional journey, the author creates a thematic structure where the decay of the plant serves as a direct reflection of the decay in personal relationships caused by neglect. Thus, the structural progression from growth to wilting reinforces the central argument that neglect impacts both nature and human bonds.
